Cc: FinPay Support <ops@finpay.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Brief outage during regional failover — timeline and ask

Hi Tessa,

During a routine failover today at 11:47 UTC FinPay observed a spike in 503 responses and a sustained availability drop for approximately 12 minutes (11:47–11:59 UTC). Rough summary from our side:

- Overall success rate for API calls to /v1/generate dropped from ~99.94% to ~60% during the window.
- Errors were 503 Service Unavailable and a subset of requests returned early timeouts.
- We traced some requests going to a fallback route that appears misconfigured — the regional routing rule sent traffic to an incompatible model shard.

We need Redwood to:
1) confirm the exact service-availability window on your side (start/end UTC) and whether this meets the SLA definition of an availability gap;
2) provide the raw trace bundle and any SRE notes that led you to the routing decision;
3) propose an initial remediation/credit path while we evaluate business impact — this incident affected checkout traffic during a high-volume batch.

Attached is a short CSV with our failed-request samples (request ids and timestamps). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alejandro Ramos
Head of Platform Reliability
FinPay

Alejandro — following internal validation from SRE (summary below) and our incident runbook, we've confirmed the event and are proposing an initial remedy.

SRE summary (Laura B.):
- Timeline (UTC): routing anomaly observed at 11:46:52, widespread 503 spike starting 11:47:03, partial recovery beginning 11:58:30, normal routing restored by 11:59:15. Total elevated-error window ~11:47:03–11:59:15 (approximately 12 minutes).
- Cause: an automated regional failover executed and a stale routing rule (stale cache in control-plane) directed ~38% of traffic to a model shard that was in a maintenance state (no warmed KV cache). That shard returned early 503s and rapid timeouts. The control-plane cache refresh laged ~70 seconds due to a backoff loop triggered by an unrelated telemetry spike.
- Mitigation applied: manual cache refresh and targeted rollback to prior routing rule at 11:58:30; autoscaler did not evict capacity during the window.

Impact & SLA qualification:
- We classify this as an availability degradation under Section 3.2 (unplanned, provider-controlled routing failure).
- Based on your monthly committed capacity and the length of the window, a prorated credit is applicable under your SLA.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Attached: trace_bundle_FINPAY_20260315.tar.gz — authoritative request logs, routing headers, and LB events; provisional_credit_calc_FINPAY.xlsx — draft prorated credit calculation (assumptions are in the notes tab).
2) Proposed provisional credit: USD 9,600 (prorated for the impacted minutes against your monthly committed fee). This is preliminary pending any additional evidence from FinPay.
3) Postmortem: our SRE team will prepare a short RCA (1–2 pages) and a remediation plan (control-plane cache hardening + an additional pre-warm step during failovers). We propose to share the RCA by 2026-03-19 EOD.

Please confirm:
- Whether the attached traces and timeline align with your observations.
- Acceptance of the provisional credit figure or if you'd like us to hold while you pull additional samples.
- If you prefer a joint call to walk through traces and the remediation plan, we can schedule for tomorrow.

Apologies for the disruption — we own this and will prioritize the RCA and fixes.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
